primary_authorities.title: Termination of rental agreement
supports: Residential termination notice rules distinguish landlord noncompliance, nonpayment, curable noncompliance, and specified serious or repeated noncompliance; notice and cure rules depend on the subsection and facts.

primary_authorities.title: Termination of tenancy without specific term
supports: Periodic residential tenancies without a specific duration have distinct year-to-year, quarter-to-quarter, month-to-month, and week-to-week notice periods.

primary_authorities.title: Defenses to action for rent or possession; procedure
supports: Florida rent-registry procedure is an outcome-sensitive part of possession litigation and must be applied with its statutory conditions rather than universalized as an unconditional deposit rule.

primary_authorities.title: Restoration of possession to landlord
supports: After judgment for the landlord, the clerk issues a writ to the sheriff; the sheriff puts the landlord in possession after 24 hours notice conspicuously posted on the premises, and weekends and legal holidays do not stay that 24-hour period.

primary_authorities.title: Retaliatory conduct
supports: Retaliation protections depend on good-faith tenant conduct and statutory conditions; an eviction following a complaint is not automatically retaliatory.

primary_authorities.title: Prohibited practices
supports: Covered residential landlords may not interrupt tenant utilities, prevent reasonable access by lockout, or remove specified building components or tenant property except within statutory exceptions and lawful process.

primary_authorities.title: Termination of rental agreement by a servicemember
supports: Qualifying servicemembers may terminate a rental agreement under specified Florida statutory conditions using written notice and required military documentation; this state right is distinct from federal SCRA protections.

primary_authorities.title: Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act
supports: The Florida statutory PTFA provision addresses bona fide tenants, a 90-day notice-to-vacate protection, lease-term protection, and an owner-occupancy purchaser exception, subject to statutory applicability.

local_variation.statewide_rule: Chapter 83 supplies statewide residential rules, while local court forms, clerk requirements, and sheriff execution practices may vary and must be verified for the actual county/court.

nonpayment_notice.label: I RECEIVED A RENT-DEMAND / NONPAYMENT NOTICE
nonpayment_notice.description: Florida nonpayment notice is a distinct §83.56 route. The exact clock must preserve statutory trigger, service, and day-count semantics.

required_actions.text: Preserve the notice, lease, payment records, and proof of how and when the notice was delivered.

possession_consequences: Expiration of a valid notice may permit the landlord to file a possession action; the notice itself is not a sheriff eviction.

lease_violation_curable.label: I RECEIVED A NOTICE FOR A CURABLE LEASE VIOLATION
lease_violation_curable.description: Curable noncompliance is kept separate from serious/noncurable and repeated conduct under §83.56.

lease_violation_serious_repeat.label: I RECEIVED A NOTICE FOR SERIOUS OR REPEATED CONDUCT
lease_violation_serious_repeat.description: Serious/noncurable and repeated noncompliance must not inherit the curable-notice model without subsection-level verification.

periodic_termination.label: I RECEIVED A TERMINATION / NONRENEWAL NOTICE
periodic_termination.description: For a tenancy without a specific duration, §83.57 uses tenancy-period-specific written notice rules; lawful termination and later court eviction are separate events.

other_clocks.label: year-to-year
other_clocks.trigger: before the end of an annual period
other_clocks.display: At least 60 days before the end of the annual period.

other_clocks.label: quarter-to-quarter
other_clocks.trigger: before the end of a quarterly period
other_clocks.display: At least 30 days before the end of the quarterly period.

other_clocks.label: month-to-month
other_clocks.trigger: before the end of a monthly period
other_clocks.display: At least 30 days before the end of the monthly period.

other_clocks.label: week-to-week
other_clocks.trigger: before the end of a weekly period
other_clocks.display: At least 7 days before the end of the weekly period.

exceptions: Applies to tenancy without a specific duration as defined by the statute; fixed-duration agreements require separate analysis.

eviction_summons_complaint.label: I RECEIVED AN EVICTION SUMMONS + COMPLAINT
eviction_summons_complaint.description: Court-stage possession procedure is separate from the pre-suit notice. Response and rent-registry clocks remain null until exact current statute/rule/form computation is fully traced.
eviction_summons_complaint.court_or_forum: Florida county court / court identified on summons

required_actions.text: Read the summons immediately, preserve proof of service, and identify every stated response and rent-registry requirement.

possession_consequences: Failure to satisfy applicable court-stage requirements can create default or possession consequences.
exceptions: Rent-registry requirements are statutory and fact-dependent; do not assume every tenant always deposits every amount claimed without reviewing §83.60 and the case papers.

default_or_judgment.label: A DEFAULT WAS REQUESTED / ENTERED OR I LOST THE EVICTION CASE
default_or_judgment.description: Default, final judgment for possession, writ issuance, and sheriff execution are distinct procedural events.

writ_of_possession.label: A WRIT OF POSSESSION WAS ISSUED
writ_of_possession.description: After judgment for the landlord, the clerk issues a writ to the sheriff; statewide statute requires 24 hours notice conspicuously posted before the sheriff restores possession.

required_actions.text: Treat a posted writ as an immediate housing emergency; read the posted notice and contact legal/housing help at once.

immediate_clock.label: sheriff writ posting period
immediate_clock.trigger: conspicuous posting of the writ notice on the premises
immediate_clock.display: The sheriff is commanded to put the landlord in possession after 24 hours notice is conspicuously posted; Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays do not stay this 24-hour period.

possession_consequences: After the statutory posting period, the sheriff may execute the writ and restore possession to the landlord.

self_help_lockout.label: THE LANDLORD LOCKED ME OUT WITHOUT COURT PROCESS
self_help_lockout.description: Florida prohibits covered landlords from preventing reasonable tenant access, including changing locks, outside lawful possession procedures.
exceptions: Lawful sheriff execution and statutory exceptions are different from prohibited landlord self-help.

utility_interruption.label: THE LANDLORD SHUT OFF UTILITIES
utility_interruption.description: Florida prohibits covered landlords from directly or indirectly terminating or interrupting specified utility services furnished to the tenant.
exceptions: A utility-provider outage or lawful emergency/repair interruption must not automatically be labeled landlord misconduct without facts.

retaliation.label: I THINK THE LANDLORD IS RETALIATING
retaliation.description: Florida retaliation protection depends on good-faith protected tenant conduct and statutory causation/conditions; timing alone does not establish retaliation.

servicemember_lease_termination.label: I AM A SERVICEMEMBER AND NEED TO TERMINATE MY LEASE
servicemember_lease_termination.description: Florida provides a state-specific lease-termination route for qualifying servicemembers. It must remain separate from federal SCRA analysis.

required_actions.text: Use written termination notice and the military-order or commanding-officer documentation required by §83.682 when relying on the Florida statutory route.

immediate_clock.label: Florida servicemember termination effective-date minimum
immediate_clock.trigger: landlord receipt of the qualifying written termination notice
immediate_clock.display: For the Florida statutory route, the effective termination date stated in the notice must be at least 30 days after the landlord receives the notice, and one of the statute's qualifying conditions must apply.

exceptions: Veteran status alone does not establish eligibility; the Florida statute lists qualifying military circumstances.

ptfa_tenant_after_foreclosure.label: I AM A TENANT AND THE PROPERTY WAS FORECLOSED
ptfa_tenant_after_foreclosure.description: Florida's PTFA provision protects qualifying bona fide tenants after covered foreclosure, subject to its statutory conditions and relationship to federal law.

immediate_clock.label: bona fide tenant notice to vacate
immediate_clock.trigger: before the effective date of the successor-in-interest notice to vacate
immediate_clock.display: For a qualifying bona fide tenant within the statute, the successor in interest must provide notice to vacate at least 90 days before the effective date of that notice.

exceptions: Bona fide tenancy and statutory foreclosure coverage must be established; lease-term and owner-occupancy purchaser rules can change the result.
